title: Coordinate Gysin composition and the supported cup product
statement:
In the finite setting [def-pur-conventions], let $S$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $r\geq0$. In $E_r=\mathbf A^r_S$ with coordinates $x_1,\ldots,x_r$, put $E_j=\{x_{j+1}=\cdots=x_r=0\}$, so $E_0=S$ and $a_j:E_{j-1}\hookrightarrow E_j$ has equation $x_j=0$. Form $\Theta_r:(z_r)_*A_S\to A_{E_r}(r)[2r]$ by composing the Cartier supported morphisms along this chain exactly as in [lem-pur-flag-localized-product]. In the supported-Hom identification [lem-pur-supported-hom],
$$\Theta_r=(-1)^r\,\partial\kappa(x_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(x_r)\in H^{2r}_{E_0}(E_r,A(r)).$$
Here the $j$th factor on the right is the Kummer boundary for the divisor $\{x_j=0\}$ in the full ambient $E_r$, and the cup product is [def-pur-supported-cup]. Equivalently, when the frame construction [def-pur-frame-class] is read with its rank parameter instantiated by $r$ (independently of the coefficient index), this is $(-1)^r$ times the ordered coordinate frame class for the smooth pair $E_r\to S$, $E_0\to S$. For every morphism $S'\to S$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, the equality commutes with restriction to $S'$. For $r=0$ both maps are the identity. There is no assertion here about applying the smooth-pair frame definition to an arbitrary zero scheme.

proof.text: For each $j\geq1$ and $1\leq l\leq j$, put $D_{j,l}=V(x_l)\subset E_j$. On an affine chart these are polynomial coordinate divisors: multiplication by $x_l$ is injective by comparison of polynomial coefficients, even over a nonreduced ring. Their intersections are defined by the sums of their coordinate ideals. Write $\beta_{j,l}=-\partial\kappa(x_l)\in H^2_{D_{j,l}}(E_j,A(1))$. The corrected local-equation formula in [lem-pur-divisor-class], followed by [lem-pur-cartier-class-agreement], says that the negative boundary has supported-Hom representative $c_{D_{j,l},A}$. In particular $D_{j,j}=E_{j-1}$ and this representative is $d_j$ of [lem-pur-flag-localized-product]. These schemes are separated finite type, and coordinate divisors and their successive coordinate pullbacks remain Cartier, so the base-change assertion of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] applies whenever used below.

source.place: Step 3: coordinate comparison, corrected to the smooth zero-section pair on the total bundle

proof.text: Define $Q_j=\beta_{j,1}\cup\cdots\cup\beta_{j,j}\in H^{2j}_{E_0}(E_j,A(j))$, with $Q_0=1$ on $E_0=S$. Let $p_j:E_j\to E_{j-1}$ forget $x_j$, so $p_ja_j=\operatorname{id}$. Put $C_j=V(x_1,\ldots,x_{j-1})\subset E_j$ and $R_j=p_j^*Q_{j-1}$. By [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] and Step 1, $R_j$ is the product of the first $j-1$ coordinate classes in $E_j$, and $a_j^*R_j=Q_{j-1}$. The supports here are $p_j^{-1}(E_0)=C_j$ and $C_j\times_{E_j}E_{j-1}=E_0$. By [lem-pur-supported-hom], write its representative as $\gamma_j:P_{C_j}\to L_j$, where $P_C=(C\hookrightarrow E_j)_*A_C$ and $L_j=A_{E_j}(j-1)[2j-2]$. Thus $Q_j=R_j\cup\beta_{j,j}$. We will prove $Q_j=\Theta_j$ by induction, with both sides interpreted as morphisms on the same $E_j$.

source.place: Step 3: coordinate comparison, corrected to the smooth zero-section pair on the total bundle

proof.text:
Fix $j\geq1$ and abbreviate $X=E_j$, $D=E_{j-1}$, $a=a_j$, $P_D=a_*A_D$. Let $u:X\setminus D\hookrightarrow X$. On each affine chart $u$ is the principal open $D(x_j)$, hence is quasi-compact. The functor $a^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]; $a_*$ is exact, $a^*a_*\cong1$, and $u^*a_*=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Let
$$\rho_K:K\otimes_A^LP_D\longrightarrow a_*a^*K$$
be the symmetry-ordered projection mate $\pi_{a;A_D,K}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. This is an isomorphism for the objects used here. Indeed $P_D$ is flat by [def-pur-supported-cup], so the source is the termwise tensor $K^t\otimes P_D$. Its restriction to $X\setminus D$ is zero. The unit $K^t\otimes P_D\to a_*a^*(K^t\otimes P_D)$ is therefore an isomorphism by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image]. Identifying $a^*P_D=A_D$ gives the displayed target termwise. This unit composite is exactly $\rho_K$: its adjunct is the tensor comparison followed by the closed counit $a^*P_D\to A_D$, which is the defining adjunct of the projection mate. Exactness lets these termwise identifications pass to derived categories.

proof.text:
For $C=C_j$, let $\mu:P_C\otimes_A^LP_D\xrightarrow{\sim}(z_j)_*A_S$ be the specified multiplication isomorphism of [def-pur-supported-cup]. Its section formula is restriction to $E_0=C\cap D$ followed by multiplication. The same formula is the projection mate on these coefficients: its adjunct restricts the first factor to $D$ and multiplies by the second factor in $A_D$. Applying $a^*$ and using $a^*a_*\cong1$ identifies $a^*P_C$ with $(z_{j-1})_*A_S$; the resulting $\rho_{P_C}\mu^{-1}$ is the identity on $a_*(z_{j-1})_*A_S=(z_j)_*A_S$. This fixes the supported-source comparison by its quotient generators, rather than by an unspecified isomorphism. On $K=L_j$ the same projection formula is
$$\rho_{L_j}:L_j\otimes_A^LP_D\xrightarrow{\sim}a_*\bigl(A_D(j-1)[2j-2]\bigr).$$
It is the twist comparison used in [lem-pur-flag-localized-product]: locally a twist is a free rank-one degree-zero sheaf by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], and both maps send $l\otimes b$ to $b\,a^*l$. Shifts use the projection mate's shift comparison; these degree-zero sheaf maps agree on local generators and under change of basis, so sheaf gluing gives equality before shifting.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), compared with the specified multiplication of closed constants in def-pur-supported-cup; quotient-generator and twist normalization by the agent.

proof.text:
Naturality of the projection mate in $K$, applied to $\gamma_j:P_C\to L_j$, gives the typed identity
$$\rho_{L_j}(\gamma_j\otimes1_{P_D})\mu^{-1}=(a_j)_*(a_j^*\gamma_j): (z_j)_*A_S\longrightarrow(a_j)_*a_j^*L_j.$$
Here the source comparison is exactly Step 4. Functoriality of tensor [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial] factors $\gamma_j\otimes d_j$ as $(1_{L_j}\otimes d_j)(\gamma_j\otimes1_{P_D})$. Consequently the defining tensor formula in [def-pur-supported-cup] represents $Q_j=R_j\cup\beta_{j,j}$ by
$$\sigma\,(1_{L_j}\otimes d_j)\rho_{L_j}^{-1}(a_j)_*(a_j^*\gamma_j).$$
The map $\sigma$ is the specified shift comparison followed by twist multiplication. By Step 4 the first three factors are precisely $d_j(j-1)[2j-2]$. To order the factors as in that notation use tensor symmetry: its sign is $(-1)^{(2j-2)2}=1$, and the shift comparisons are those of [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus]. We have therefore proved the actual nested-composition formula
$$[Q_j]=d_j(j-1)[2j-2]\circ(a_j)_*(a_j^*\gamma_j).$$

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), naturality of its adjunct; signed tensor-morphism calculation as specified by lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus.

proof.text:
For $j=0$, $Q_0$ and $\Theta_0$ are both $\operatorname{id}_{A_S}$. Suppose $[Q_{j-1}]=\Theta_{j-1}$ as morphisms on $E_{j-1}$. Pulling the tensor-morphism representative of $R_j$ back along $a_j$ gives the representative of $a_j^*R_j=Q_{j-1}$: inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] and commutes with tensor and shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], and the source multiplication comparison is the one checked in Step 4. Equivalently this follows factor by factor from [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] and the explicit cup definition. Thus $a_j^*\gamma_j=\Theta_{j-1}$, as an equality on $E_{j-1}$. Apply the exact functor $(a_j)_*$ to this equality. Step 5 now gives
$$[Q_j]=d_j(j-1)[2j-2]\circ(a_j)_*\Theta_{j-1}=\Theta_j,$$
where the last equality is the recurrence in [lem-pur-flag-localized-product]. No equality is inferred on $E_j$ merely from an equality after restriction to $E_{j-1}$: the specified pushforward and then $d_j$ are applied to both sides. At $j=r$, $Q_r$ is the product of the negatives of the full ambient coordinate boundaries. Bilinearity of the supported cup product gives $Q_r=(-1)^r\,\partial\kappa(x_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(x_r)$; [lem-pur-supported-hom] gives the asserted cohomology equality.

proof.text: For the frame interpretation, $E_r\to S$ is smooth of relative dimension $r$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], and $E_0=S\to S$ is smooth of relative dimension zero. These schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied over the field $k$. At $z\in E_0$ the successive coordinate quotients of $\mathcal O_{E_r,z}$ are the corresponding local rings of the coordinate subspaces. Each coordinate lies in the maximal ideal and is a nonzerodivisor, since the same is true in the polynomial ring before localization and after quotienting by any preceding coordinates. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] at each quotient gives $\dim\mathcal O_{E_r,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{S,z}+r$. Hence the pure-codimension hypothesis in [def-pur-frame-class] holds. With its geometric rank parameter named $r$, independently of the coefficient index, the ordered coordinate frame defines the product of the positive boundaries by that definition, so $Q_r$ is $(-1)^r$ times that frame class. The empty frame for $r=0$ gives the identity, as does the nested construction.

source.place: Step 3: coordinate comparison, corrected to the smooth zero-section pair on the total bundle

proof.text: Let $S'\to S$ be a morphism as in the statement and $v:E'_r\to E_r$ its affine-space base change. The coordinate divisor $D_{r,l}$ pulls back to $D'_{r,l}$, again Cartier. By [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] and [lem-pur-cartier-class-agreement], $v^*\beta_{r,l}=\beta'_{r,l}$. The pullback and cup identities of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] give $v^*Q_r=Q'_r$. Apply the already established equality both over $S$ and over $S'$ to obtain $v^*\Theta_r=v^*Q_r=Q'_r=\Theta'_r$ under the same supported-source and twist comparisons. This proves restriction compatibility without assuming that restriction from a closed subspace detects a morphism.

We have therefore proved the actual nested-composition formula
$$[Q_j]=d_j(j-1)[2j-2]\circ(a_j)_*(a_j^*\gamma_j).$$

For $j=0$, $Q_0$ and $\Theta_0$ are both $\operatorname{id}_{A_S}$. Suppose $[Q_{j-1}]=\Theta_{j-1}$ as morphisms on $E_{j-1}$. Pulling the tensor-morphism representative of $R_j$ back along $a_j$ gives the representative of $a_j^*R_j=Q_{j-1}$: inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] and commutes with tensor and shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], and the source multiplication comparison is the one checked in Step 4. Equivalently this follows factor by factor from [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] and the explicit cup definition. Thus $a_j^*\gamma_j=\Theta_{j-1}$, as an equality on $E_{j-1}$. Apply the exact functor $(a_j)_*$ to this equality. Step 5 now gives
$$[Q_j]=d_j(j-1)[2j-2]\circ(a_j)_*\Theta_{j-1}=\Theta_j,$$
where the last equality is the recurrence in [lem-pur-flag-localized-product]. No equality is inferred on $E_j$ merely from an equality after restriction to $E_{j-1}$: the specified pushforward and then $d_j$ are applied to both sides. At $j=r$, $Q_r$ is exactly the product of the full ambient coordinate boundaries required by the statement; [lem-pur-supported-hom] gives the asserted cohomology equality.

old_proof.text: For the frame interpretation, $E_r\to S$ is smooth of relative dimension $r$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], and $E_0=S\to S$ is smooth of relative dimension zero. These schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied over the field $k$. At $z\in E_0$ the successive coordinate quotients of $\mathcal O_{E_r,z}$ are the corresponding local rings of the coordinate subspaces. Each coordinate lies in the maximal ideal and is a nonzerodivisor, since the same is true in the polynomial ring before localization and after quotienting by any preceding coordinates. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] at each quotient gives $\dim\mathcal O_{E_r,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{S,z}+r$. Hence the pure-codimension hypothesis in [def-pur-frame-class] holds. With its geometric rank parameter named $r$, independently of the coefficient index, the ordered coordinate frame defines exactly $Q_r$ by that definition. The empty frame for $r=0$ gives the identity, as does the nested construction.

By [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] and [lem-pur-cartier-class-agreement], $v^*\beta_{r,l}=\beta'_{r,l}$. The pullback and cup identities of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] give $v^*Q_r=Q'_r$. Apply the already established equality both over $S$ and over $S'$ to obtain $v^*\Theta_r=v^*Q_r=Q'_r=\Theta'_r$ under the same supported-source and twist comparisons. This proves restriction compatibility without assuming that restriction from a closed subspace detects a morphism.
